punchline: A questionnaire about childhood, answered by 17,000 patients, turned out to be linked to their health as adults.
thirty_sec: More than 17,000 members of a health plan answered questions about hard experiences in childhood. The more they reported, the more health and emotional problems they tended to have later. Van der Kolk reads this as a brain that adapted to a frightening home by staying on alert, which helps there and can cause trouble later, though he treats these patterns as changeable.
